records.author: Communications All Saints'
heading_structure: h1: Praying for the Persecuted Church: Ukraine
records.body_text:
Communications All Saints'
September 23, 2026
prayer
Praying for the Persecuted Church: Ukraine
Communications All Saints'
September 23, 2026
prayer
During the conflict in Ukraine, Barnabas Aid has been helping suffering Christians with food (three-months' supply) for 560 families, along with hygiene kits for 320 families. Donations also covered house repairs for five families. Pray that God will continue to sustain and encourage His Church in Ukraine.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Ukraine.
Week of 9/27/26: Mali, West Africa
Al Qaeda-affiliated militants (terrorists) in Mali recently increased the amount of territory they hold. The ultimate goal of these Islamist terrorists is to take over several countries in West Africa. While there are not a lot of Christians in Mali (about 2%), everyone is precious to Jesus, and all need our prayers.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mali, West Africa.
Week of 9/20/26: Chibok, Borno State, Nigeria
Praise God that 6,000 Christians in this Nigerian state have recently been reached with food through Barnabas Aid. The recipients are those severely affected by Islamist terrorism in northeastern Nigeria. Because of violence and instability, farmers have not been able to grow food. Pray for these precious people who have suffered so much.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Chibok, Borno State, Nigeria.
Week of 9/13/26: Yemen
A young woman from a Muslim background was recently converted to Christ. Now she prays for the conversions of her family members. Christian converts in Yemen are hated by the Muslim majority as apostates. In addition millions suffer from severe humanitarian needs such as food shortages. Pray for Christians who risk even their lives for the sake of their faith.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Yemen.
Week of 9/6/26: North Korea
North Korean authorities boast that they have virtually eliminated all religion. The experts in South Korea do not believe this: "We know there are still strong Christians who are worshiping in small groups or as individuals." The Church cannot be defeated by the powers of darkness, but we must continue to pray for them as they endure unthinkable hardships for the Name of Christ.
Pray for our persecuted brothers and sisters in North Korea.
Week of 8/30/26: The Philippines
Two islands in the Philippines were the worst-affected in the region by unprecedented tropical storms in the fall of 2025. These storms caused widespread destruction and hundreds of deaths. Barnabas Aid provided urgently needed food and clean drinking water for 2,110 Christian families. Pray for these families to be spiritually strengthened as they continue to recover from their ordeal.
Pray for our suffering brothers and sisters in the Philippines.
Week of 8/23/26: Iraq
Due to remarriage, it is not unusual for someone born as a Christian in Iraq to have to change their official religion from Islam back to Christianity. Normally, this is extremely difficult, but recently the court in Iraq allowed a young woman to have her court records amended so that her papers now say she is Christian. Join her in praising God for this unusual ruling.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iraq who are under similar circumstances.
Week of 8/16/26: Iran
As you can imagine, the Church in Iran is suffering greatly. They are under political pressure, fear, and surveillance. When Christians are caught, especially pastors and leaders, they are usually put in the notorious Evin Prison, from which most are either severely persecuted or killed.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran.
Week of 8/9/2026: Pakistan
Most Christians in Pakistan live way beneath the poverty line — many suffer to get adequate food.
Those who give to Barnabas Aid provide monthly dollars which help the Christian community in Pakistan survive. Many are what is known as “Brick Kiln Workers,” where families are bonded to the owners for generations. Barnabas Aid has gradually over the years been able to free some of them. It is nearly impossible to express the level of their gratitude.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Pakistan.
Week of 8/2/26: China
Over the past several years, the Chinese Church has become subject to increasing restriction and regulation, including church leaders, who must “love the motherland, support the leadership of the Communist Party of China, and practice the core values of socialism.” As a result, the Three-Self Protestant Church enjoys less freedom, while unofficial “house churches” are targeted by the authorities. Many pastors have been tortured, imprisoned, punished with severe physical work, and even killed outright. Pray that the church will be able to successfully navigate these sevee legal restrictions.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in China.
Week of 7/26/26: Sri Lanka
Christians are a marginalized and persecuted group in Buddhist-majority Sri Lanka. Local authorities and Buddhist extremists, including monks, perpetuate the false idea that Christian worship is forbidden without permission. Service and prayer meetings are routinely shut down, even in private homes. Converts are particularly targeted. Pray for the Lord to protect pastors and congregations, and for courage and perseverance for all Christians
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Sri Lanka.
Week of 7/19/26: Egypt
Many Christian families in Egypt struggle with poverty and rising living costs, especially in remote and underserved areas where access to food is limited. Recent gifts through Barnabas Aid brought relief. Pray that such acts of love will strengthen faith, develop community, and shine as a witness to their neighbors of Christ’s compassion. Ask the Lord to continue sustaining the Church in Egypt, enabling them to remain steadfast.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Egypt.
Week of 7/12/26: Nepal
The church in Nepal faces extreme poverty, social stigma, exclusion, and disadvantage both for their “low caste” status and their faith in Christ. Aid projects through Barnabas Aid provide schooling and vocational training and shelter for at-risk girls and women who have suffered abuse. Pray that this work will be a blessing to marginalized Nepali Christians, and that it would strengthen the Church.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Nepal.
Week of 7/5/26: Bangladesh
Recent elections have given God’s church in Bangladesh hope as no Islamist parties gained a majority. However, the Islamists continue to harass believers. Four evangelists in the north were captured and held by police. Although they were eventually released, they were threatened with death, and that is no idle threat!
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Bangladesh.
Week of 6/28/26: Afghanistan
The Taliban government in early 2026 strengthened legal discrimination against religious minorities. Only followers of the Hanafi school of Islamic jurisprudence are recognized as “true Muslims” — those who practice any other religion or belief are now labeled as being “innovators” or “heretics.” This code prescribes death for those who share or hold “beliefs contrary to Islam.” Christians and others will be killed if their faith is discovered. Pray that the Lord will strengthen the spirit of His people as they endure such severe opposition. It is not known how many Christians there are in Afghanistan, as they must remain in strict hiding.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Afghanistan.
Week of 6/21/26: Syria
The Church in Syria — in spite of ongoing conflict and social instability — remains a sustaining presence in the culture. Many believers continue to face displacement, economic hardship, and insecurity. For this reason, local churches remain places of refuge, fellowship, and hope. Pray for protection, provision, and encouragement for families and leaders — especially in those areas still affected by violence. Pray for unity among believers and for the Church to shine as a light of Christs' peace and compassion.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Syria.
Week of 6/14/26: Iraq
Believers in Iraq have grown from an estimated 250 in 2010 to 3,500 today, yet they remain less than 1% of the population. Ask God to break through hearts hardened by long-standing divisions and intense rivalries, and for the successful registration of evangelical churches in Iraq. Pray especially for growth, maturity and unity among Kurdish and Yazidi believers in the north, and that local churches will continue to shine for the Gospel.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iraq.
Week of 6/7/26: Iran
As we know, the ongoing conflict in Iran is causing untold misery, and the Christians are suffering more than others. They long for freedom to share the Gospel with their neighbors and to worship freely, but hold out little hope. Pray that the Lord will draw near to His people across the wider Middle East. Pray that they remember that no matter the events of this world, His Word “is eternal; it stands firm in the heavens.” (Psalm 119:89)
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran.
Week of 5/31/26: Mozambique
Pastor Gabriel says, “The extremists are against the Gospel. If they find that you are a Christian, they will kill you.” Tens of thousands escaped the brutal insurgency being waged by Islamic State terrorists in the north. Pastor Gabriel planted a church in a settlement camp for displaced persons farther in the south which reverberates with singing and dancing. They have little, but are rich in their trust of the Lord. Pray for their well-being and for an end to the brutal efforts by the Islamic State. (Muslims believe that if they kill a Christian, it will be a guarantee that they will get into heaven - a false belief, but to them a real one!)
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mozambique.
Week of 5/24/26: Algeria
Pastor Youssef Ourahmane has been arrested for leading his protestant church in Algeria. He converted from Islam in 1977 and has now led a church for three decades. His conviction is for “illegal worship,” even though Algeria’s constitution says it protects free speech and religious freedom. However, Algeria has other repressive laws that violate the rights of Christians and other religious minorities. He is appealing his conviction before the Supreme Court of Algeria and is only the latest of many to be convicted. Although his church has been closed, he continues to support his congregation. Alliance Defending Freedom is arguing his case at the Supreme Court.
Pray for Pastor Youssef and the other Christians in Algeria, and pray for the work of the Alliance Defending Freedom.
Week of 5/10/26: Iran
Pray for two Iranian Christians and converts from Islam who are involved in a house church. Hanna and Daniel received two-year sentences in July 2024 and began their sentences in mid-November 2025. Prison conditions in Iran are horrific. Pray that Daniel and Hannah will know the Lord’s presence and comfort.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran who are converts from Islam
Week of 5/3/26: Myanmar
Pray for the believers in Falam Township, Chin State, Myanmar.
A church building and 20 houses were recently destroyed by the Tatmadaw (Myanmar military) bombing. This attack came days after another bombing destroyed seven homes. Please pray for God's comfort and provision for our brothers and sisters.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Myanmar.
Week of 4/26/26: Mozambique
Islamists are encroaching more and more into the north of the country, attacking homes and church buildings. At least 27 Christians were brutally killed in the last two months of 2025. Pray for our brothers and sisters who have been left bereaved, traumatized, injured, and displaced.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mozambique.
Week of 4/19/26: Nigeria
Pray for Nigerian Christians who are under continual attack from Fulani Islamists. Pray especially for the recovery of a church in Kwara State, the attack of which was inadvertently live-streamed because the church was attacked in the middle of a service.
Three victims were killed, and a young girl who suffered a severe wound to her neck continues to be in critical condition. The live-stream showed people attempting to escape.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 4/12/26: Refugees in Iran
Pray for Tymour Hosseini. an Afghan refugee in Iran who has begun a two-year sentence for his involvement in a house church. He has lived in Iran for about 20 years, is married and has two children. The Iranian authorities consider involvement in unofficial churches as anti-state activity and a crime against national security. Pray for the Lord to be his refuge and strength as he endures this ordeal.
Pray for our brothers and sisters who are refugees in Iran.
Week of 4/5/26: Myanmar
Several Christian tribes in Myanmar are under severe persecution by the Tatmandow military. The villages and churches are continuously under attack, and even when they escape into the jungle they are pursued and bombed. Their healthcare system has completely collapsed. Barnabas Aid funds a Christian-led teaching hospital and trauma center, providing free 24-hour medical care. Pray for the wounded, those in pregnancy, and for the children who suffer inordinately. Give thanks for this. hospital.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Myanmar (Burma)
Week of 3/29/26: Iran
As you know, there was severe persecution in January in Iran. The church is growing rapidly there, especially among Muslim-background believers. Any Christians are vulnerable to imprisonment in severe conditions and are likely to be shot. All Christians in Iran are treated with suspicion and hostility as apostates from Islam. Farsi (Persian)-speaking Christians are automatically considered to be enemies of the state. Pray for all Christians in Iran, especially those accused falsely of crimes against national security.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran.
Week of 3/22/26: Uganda
Barnabas Aid recently gave 365 young Christians in Uganda their first Bibles. In a Muslim-majority area of Uganda, persecution is a constant threat. As a result of the Bibles, the attendance of young people has also increased at local churches. Give thanks that these young people now have a way to learn more about Jesus.
Pray for our young brothers and sisters in Uganda.
Week of 3/15/26: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
Eight Christians were recently beheaded by ISCAP (Islamic State Central Africa Province) in northeast DRC. It was an armed assault, and ISCAP killed around 800 Christians in their rampage. Anti-terrorist experts say it is clear that the Islamists are explicitly targeting Christians over their faith. Ask God to give courage to His people in the DRC.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in the DRC.
Week of 3/8/26: North Korea
North Korea is considered the most brutal place to try to survive as a Christian. It faces unprecedented threats in terms of information in-flow. Among the information breaching the borders of this repressive, totalitarian state is the Word of God, as digital copies of the Scriptures are smuggled across the border. Pray for the safety of those risking their lives to bring God’s Word to North Korea and ask that the underground churches of North Korea be strengthened and more people come to know Jesus as their Savior.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in North Korea.
Week of 3/1/26: China
Recently, 30 Christians and their founding pastor were arrested and are being imprisoned.
Their founding pastor was accused on suspicion of using “illegal information networks.” Pastor Jin Mingri was the founder of Zion Church in 2007, which has both an online and in-person congregation. Such churches are illegal in China as all must agree to the Communist format which insists that they teach the principles of communism in their churches, holding up the Chinese Communist leaders as, basically, superior to Jesus. Such actions by the state only seem to cause more rapid growth of the Chinese Church.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in China.
Week of 2/22/26: South Sudan
Recently, one elderly widow in South Sudan said, “I have lived many years, but I have never seen a day like this. For weeks, I survived by eating wild leaves and prayer.” She had received a food box from Western Christians through Barnabas Aid. Vulnerable Christian families in this famine-stricken country are being helped by the greater church as they struggle with civil war and acute poverty.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in South Sudan.
Week of 2/15/26: Nigeria
Last summer 6,500 Christians were displaced and 200 killed in less than 24 hours of violence in Benue state. One village elder, Amos, lost his wife and all but one of his children. Pastor Musa lost nine family members in the attack. Pray that even as they mourn, bereaved families will draw strength in knowing that their loved ones are safe in the Lord's hands. Pray for increased protection and justice from the Nigerian government.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 2/8/26: Pakistan
Thank God that recently a 72-year-old Christian has been released after spending 23 years on death row in Lahore, Pakistan. He was imprisoned for supposed “blasphemy” against Muhammad. In most cases, these accusations are completely unfounded and are the result of extreme Islamic prejudice against Christians. Pray for this man (and the entire Christian community in Lahore) to be protected and safe since his acquittal, and that the police will be proactive in protecting him and them.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Lahore, Pakistan.
Week of 2/1/26: Iran
Because of the huge protest in Iran right now, and the violence of the Theocracy against any of their people (Christian or not), extra prayer is needed for all citizens of Iran. Estimates of those dead, injured, or imprisoned (and probably subsequently hanged) increase daily. Pray for the people of Iran to have courage in the face of such violence and terror by their own government, especially for Muslim Background Believers.
Pray for all the people of Iran, but especially our brothers and sisters in Christ.
Week of 1/25/26: Iraqi Kurdistan
Many MBBs (Muslim background believers) suffer severe repression in Iran, so Iraqi Kurdistan is a far safer environment for ALL Christians, not just MBBs. Ask the Lord to provide for their needs in this community. They need legal recognition and financial support as they try to re-establish themselves in a new nation.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iraqi Kurdistan.
Week of 1/18/26: Sri Lanka
A group of Buddhist monks in Sri Lanka continues to prevent churches (especially small house churches) from meeting for worship. The police sometimes protect Christians in these situations, but then turn on them and blame them for the escalating situation. Please pray for divine protection, spiritual strength, and unwavering faith for our brothers and sisters in this difficult situation.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Sri Lanka
Week of 1/11/26: Tunisia
Tunisia has a young and growing Christian community, including many indigenous believers from Muslim backgrounds and immigrant Christians who are active in sharing their faith despite legal and social challenges. Pray for the protection of churches meeting in homes. Pray that God would bring a deeper understanding of His love and truth in this predominantly Sunni Muslim country.
Pray for the young Christians, our brothers and sisters, in Tunisia.
Week of 12/28/25: Lebanon
Pray for all the people in Lebanon who are struggling with a deep and long-lasting economic crisis. Ask God to provide political leaders who will provide honesty, unity, and wise governance.
Ask God to strengthen and encourage the Christian Community who are weary and need hope, peace, and healing as they deal with their highly dysfunctional country.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Lebanon.
Week of 12/21/25: Sri Lanka
Recently, a group of Buddhist monks interrupted church meetings in a pastor’s home in Sri Lanka;  then they returned later and interrupted them again. The authorities will do nothing about this. Pray for the police to be willing to help the churches in Sri Lanka!
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Sri Lanka
Week of 12/14/25: Pakistan
Recent devastating floods in Pakistan have led to more than 250 deaths and left hundreds more homeless. Thirty Christian families’ homes of brick and mud were washed away by the raging floodwaters. Pray for the success of the humanitarian response to this latest natural disaster. Pray especially for Barnabas Aid project partners to be able to supply food, medical supplies, and safe drinking water to the flood victims.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Pakistan.
Week of 12/7/25: The Sahel (West Africa)
Al Qaeda launched more than 12 attacks on targets in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger this summer. These were part of a surge in attacks across the Sahel that is a concrete effort to create a parallel Islamic state from western Mali to southern Niger and northern Benin. It is estimated that they already control 60% of Burkina Faso. Ask for the Lord to protect Christian communities in the Sahel and across West Africa.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in the Sahel.
Week of 11/23/25: Plateau State, Nigeria
Recently, 30 armed Fulani Islamists attacked a village in Plateau State. They came in the early hours of the morning, shooting and setting houses ablaze. A three-year-old girl and nine members of a local pastor’s family were burned alive in their home. Pray that Pastor Musa will be comforted by the Lord for his great loss and that the shock and outrage at the killings would lead to great urgency by authorities to take decisive action.
Pray for our suffering brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 11/16/25: South Sudan
In the midst of a horrific civil war, South Sudanese Christians are suffering extreme poverty, often surviving on what one widow described as wild leaves and prayer! Barnabas Aid recently delivered food for 250 households. Pray that they will continue to provide for many more Christian families in such dire circumstances.
Pray for our suffering brothers and sisters in South Sudan.
Week of 11/9/25: Northern Ghana
Pray for the poverty-stricken area of Northern Ghana. Barnabas Aid has given 60 pigs to pastors and missionaries in Northern Ghana. To date, seven have given birth, providing necessary income while the pastors and missionaries pursue their vocations. Praise God for this project! (Barnabas Aid plans to give 1,000,000 pigs and 1,000,000 chickens to Christians in need around the world.)
Pray for this project to provide much-needed income.
Week of 11/2/25: Eritrea
The Marxist government in Eritrea continues to target Christians for arbitrary arrest and long-term detention in overcrowded and brutal prison conditions without trial. All places of worship are outlawed except Orthodox, Roman Catholic, and Lutheran as well as Sunni Islam. Over 10,000 Christians have fled this repressive Marxist system.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Eritrea.
Week of 10/26/25: Mozambique
Terrorists from the Islamic State abducted six Christians and subjected them to execution-style killing in July. The insurgents demand that Christians pay a jizya tax as a sign of their submission to Islam. Pray for this to end!
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mozambique!
Week of 10/19/25: Bangladesh
Ishrat, a Bangladeshi Muslim-background believer, suffered hardship and abuse at the hands of her own family after converting to Christianity. “The more they tried to stop me from following Jesus, the more love for Jesus was poured into my heart.” Eventually, she was expelled from the family home and from material support, yet her faith remains undiminished. “He cares for me and loves me even when my own family and friends hate me.” Praise God for her faith and example to those of us in the West.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Bangladesh.
Week of 10/12/25: Syria
A suicide bombing at a church service in Damascus left 25 worshippers dead and more than 60 injured. The attack was carried out by Islamists with links to the Islamic State. The Syrian government, while condemning the killings, has recent links with Al Qaeda, and there are ongoing concerns about its willingness to protect Christians and other religious minorities. Pray for the Lord’s protection of his people in Syria.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Syria.
Week of 10/5/25: Iran
Laleh Saati, an Iranian Christian convert from Islam, has been released from prison after serving 15 months of a two-year sentence. She was living in Malaysia for several years, where she was baptized. When she returned to Iran, she was arrested for her involvement in a “house church”; a video of her baptism was used as evidence against her. Praise the Lord that she has now been released.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran.
Week of 9/28/25: West Java, Indonesia
Pray for a Christian community in West Java where Islamist radicals protested against the proposal to designate a multipurpose building as a place of worship. It has been used by the church since 1980, while locals claim it should only be for social use. Church leaders are seeking to register the facility while keeping it open to the public. Hardliners among the Islamist radicals are creating tension and causing disturbance, especially on Christian holy days like Ash Wednesday.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in West Java.
Week of 9/21/25: West Africa
The ECOWAS (Economic Community of West Africa) Court of Justice has declared that “blasphemy” laws in Northern Nigeria violate international human rights standards, striking down section 3820(b) of the Kano State Sharia Penal Code Law that mandates the death penalty for insulting Muhammad and which imposes a prison sentence for “any religion.” Pray for the protection of Christians and others in northern Nigeria and elsewhere who are vulnerable to accusations of “blasphemy” and the mob violence that can follow.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in West Africa.
Week of 9/14/25: Nigeria
At the end of last month, two Christian education officials were killed by an IED (improvised Explosive Device) that exploded along a highway in Borno State, north-eastern Nigeria. They were transporting mangos from a major location on a key food-supply route. Ask for comfort for the young men’s families and friends as they grieve and for wisdom for the authorities in Borno State to intensify security and to protect the population from these Islamist attacks.
Pray for our persecuted brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 9/7/25: Pakistan
Young women - as young as 14 - are regularly kidnapped in Pakistan by Muslims who force them illegally to convert to Islam and to marry much older Muslim men. Recently, one young woman was able to be released after two years by Christian attorneys. She was traumatized but miraculously did not have any children and is now in trauma therapy.
Pray for our persecuted brothers and sisters in Pakistan.
Week of 8/31/25: Mauritania
An anti-Christian mob in Mauritania inflamed by anti-Christian rhetoric online exhumed a recently buried body, destroyed his tombstone, and dragged his body through the streets. Eventually, the body was reburied 12 miles away. Serious tension remains as believers are publicly labeled infidels and are shunned by relatives. Ask God to give church leaders wisdom and strength as they face such difficulties on a daily basis.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mauritania.
Week of 8/24/25: Nigeria
At least 180 Christians were killed in a wave of anti-Christian violence in Plateau State, Nigeria, in April. A community leader declared, “We are tired of burying our people every other week.” The Islamist violence is unrelenting and severe. Pray that the Name of the Lord will be a strong tower and a place of refuge to His people across Nigeria!
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 8/17/25: Laos
Four Christian families in northwestern Laos were evicted from their village in early May.
Their houses were demolished, and they were forced to abandon most of their possessions.
There have been other instances of Christians being targeted in this way in Laos. They have been supplied with rice, cooking oil, hygiene products, and other essentials through the wider Church.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Laos.
Week of 8/10/25: Myanmar
After the severe earthquake earlier this year, the Tatmadaw (Myanmar military) bombed a city where an orphanage was destroyed, sending 137 children fleeing to a town 10 days’ walk away. The leader of the orphanage said that the children were safely accommodated by a church in the town. Pray for the continued protection of orphans amid the ongoing conflict in Myanmar.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Myanmar.
Week of 8/3/25: Egypt
Lord God and Heavenly Father, thank you for the faithful work of Egyptian churches in helping our disadvantaged brothers and sisters. We pray that those they support will learn to read and write, and that these abilities will help break the cycle of poverty and marginalization. We also pray that they will be blessed and nurtured through the reading of Your holy Word, growing in faith and hope. We ask this in our Savior’s Name.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Egypt.
Week of 7/27/25: Armenia & Karabakh
There is an Armenian self-governing Christian region within Azerbaijan called Nagorno-Karabakh. Azerbaijani Muslim militants (the majority population in Azerbaijan) attacked this area in September 2023 and drove an estimated 120,000 people, almost the entire population of Karabakh, into Armenia. The few left have been imprisoned and subjected to torture and degrading treatment by the Azerbaijani military.
Pray for the release of these prisoners, for the protection of Armenia from further aggression, and for employment and well-being for those who fled and are currently in dire straits.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Armenia and Karabakh.
Week of 7/20/25: Iran
Pastor Ahmadi immigrated from Iran to Turkey in January 2024. Turkey has detained him and he faces imminent deportation back to Iran. Pastor Ahmadi, age 57, is a convert from Islam who fled persecution in Iran in 2013. Christians in Iran who have converted from Islam are under constant threat of arrest, imprisonment, and death. Pray that Pastor Ahmadi will be encouraged by his faith and the Lord’s presence with him during his ordeal and that Turkey will soon release him from detention.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iran.
Week of 7/13/25: Kyrgyzstan
New legislation came into force in Kyrgyzstan at the beginning of 2025 which has increased restrictions on freedom of religion or belief, including a ban on sharing faith in public. This legislation now requires evidence of at least 500 founding members of any church group, rather than 200, which was the previously permitted number. Pray for wisdom and discernment for church leaders to enable them to find ways for Christians to meet and worship in spite of the new restrictions. Pray against the spirit of discouragement for these leaders.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Kyrgyzstan.
Week of 7/6/25: Indonesia
Recently the Islamists in West Java held a protest against a Christian church in the process of getting a building permit, after having worshipped there since 2008. Pray that their permit will be granted quickly and that there will be greater tolerance between the Christian and Muslim communities.
Pray for the Persecuted Church in Indonesia.
Week of 6/29/25: Young Women and Girls in Northern Uganda
Five thousand young women and girls in northern Uganda have recently been trained to make reusable sanitary pads. Such items are hard to access and unreachably expensive for most families in the region. Various schools hosted the training workshops. The women can then pass on their knowledge to others. One school principal described the experience as “an awakening of hope and a birth of new dreams.” Pray that these girls will realize their potential in Christ.
Pray for our sisters in northern Uganda.
Week of 6/22/25: Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)
Confusion and internal violence in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are increasing. The Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP) is taking advantage of the confusion. ISCAP has killed at least 289 believers between Christmas 2024 and mid-March 2025. ISCAP may spare victims who convert to Islam but will kill those who cling to Jesus. Pray that the Lord will help the Christians to be brave and will sustain His people.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in the DRC.
Week of 6/15/25: Refugee Christians in the Holy Land
At least 3,000 African Christians from Eritrea, Sudan, and Ethiopia have fled to the Holy Land to escape violence and persecution in their own countries. Their needs include food, trauma counseling, afterschool programs, and assistance in resettlement applications and legal cases.
Pray for their needs to be met and that God will enable them to rebuild their lives.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in the Holy Land.
Week of 6/8/25: Syria
Christians in Syria have deep concerns for their safety after a flare-up of sectarian violence in the country’s northwest. One thousand Alawites, a Muslim sect considered to be heretical by the Sunni majority, were killed recently but at least 12 Christians were among those killed. Pray for their safety under a very unsettling situation.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Syria.
Week of 5/25/25: Lebanon
Lebanese Christians, principally in Beirut, have suffered greatly. The government is not particularly stable; Hezbollah (a radical Muslim organization formed under Iran), and the explosion in the port of Beirut around a year ago have left them desperate for food, hygiene items, and fuel. Local church pastors and leaders do what they can to support their beleaguered people.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Lebanon.
Week of 5/18/25: Algeria
The authorities in Algeria have been guilty of “unlawful church closures and unjustified arrests and imprisonments of pastors,” according to human rights experts. Algeria’s evangelical Christian community has been under duress since 2017 with more than 40 church buildings having been closed and also restrictions on holding church meetings or services in private homes.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Algeria.
Week of 5/11/25: Cuba
Christians and citizens in Cuba are under a severe food shortage verging on famine.
Recently Barnabas Aid (a Christian supporter of the persecuted church) was able to send Cuba's Christians a four-foot container of food from the United States which has brought relief to their dire situation. Pray for increased harvest and an end to food shortage.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Cuba.
Week of 5/4/25: Nigeria
There were 72 people killed in Plateau State in Nigeria over Easter.
The killings, fires, and brutalities were carried out by the Fulani Muslim herdsmen,
ostensibly
to obtain more land for their cattle. Thousands of Nigerians also carried out a peaceful march to Government House in Jos, the capital, to call upon the government to provide protection before these events take place, not afterward. The President is Muslim and the government seems not to care about the death toll. Pastor Amos Mohzo said, “We are tired of these mass killings. Enough is enough!”
Pray for our suffering brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 4/27/25: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia is the birthplace of Islam and contains the cities considered to be the most holy to the religion: Mecca and Medina. Sharia (Islamic law) is strictly enforced and leaving Islam is punishable by death. Christians are banned from publicly practicing their religion. Saudi Arabia's inhabitants who believe must be secret Christians. Pray that they will be strong in their faith and Jesus will watch over them and keep them safe.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Saudi Arabia.
Week of 4/20/25: Venezuela
There has been an intense government crackdown on non-governmental organizations (NGOs). In August 2024, 1,650 churches and Christian NGOs were forced to close. Pray that the Holy Spirit will draw near to Christians in Venezuela.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Venezuela.
Week of 4/13/25: The Sahel
The “Sahel” is composed of several nations: Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger as well as other countries. The Church in Mali is
very small
. These Christians are under a high-alert level of food insecurity, meaning that famine has become a severe possibility. The situation is largely driven by conflict caused by Islamist terrorists who are active in the region. Their food insecurity is such that 1.4 million people in Mali are on course to suffer “acute food insecurity” and 120,000 are at risk of “emergency levels.” Ask the Lord to provide for the hungry and bring peace to these troubled lands.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger as well as other countries in the region of the Sahel.
Week of 4/6/25: Uzbekistan
Recently the church in Uzbekistan has benefited from regular training opportunities for church leaders. Their ages range from 65 to 15 and they are involved in various ministries — teachers, worship leaders, prayer group and house church leaders, children and youth workers, as well as evangelists. Give thanks for these leaders and their training. Pray that each participant in the training will effectively apply what they learn as they build up the Body of Christ.
Pray for our Uzbekistan brothers and sisters.
Week of 3/30/25: Pakistan
Many Christians in Pakistan suffer under the charge of “blasphemy” against Islam, particularly against Mohammad and the Quran. Most of these Christians are illiterate. Many Christians in Pakistan are under the yoke of debt and bonded labor. Their livelihood is working as brick kiln workers whose loans — taken out at times of crisis from their owners — have led to them and their families being trapped almost as slaves. Give thanks that a Christian organization, Barnabas Aid, has been able to free many of these families. Give thanks for those who have been freed and those who have been occasionally acquitted in the courts.
Pray for our Pakistani brothers and sisters.
Week of 3/23/25: Kazakhstan
Many Christians in Kazakhstan are mostly poor and are often denied employment because of their faith. Many are converts from Islam who have to keep their faith secret, even from their own families. There is often no money or materials for outreach, which is strictly monitored, or to repair or build new churches. Yet the Kazakh church's love for Jesus means they remain grateful and passionate about Him.
Pray for our Kazakh brothers and sisters.
Week of 3/16/25: Nigeria
Nigerian Christians suffer persecution across their nation, but particularly in the north with the incursion of militant Islamic terrorists. Recently Northern Plateau State has been particularly hard hit. Several churches and Christian schools have been damaged. A school building collapsed. killing 22 students and severely injuring others. At least one church and school are without electricity in a particularly remote part of this state. Also in Niger State a church building was burned down by unidentified arsonists. These situations plus kidnappings of pastors and church leaders by militant Islam make being a Christian in Nigeria require extraordinary courage, strength, and faith.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Week of 3/9/25: Myanmar (Burma)
The ongoing conflict in Myanmar is the result of the Tatmadaw (Myanmar military). They are Buddhist and have caused endless suffering to the church for years. They are particularly against certain Christian tribal groups (the Karen for example). They bomb churches and “chase” IDPs (internally displaced persons) into the jungles, killing and injuring many. Recently, in Mon Hla village, one whole side of a church building was destroyed in a bombing raid, as was most of the village. Residents were twice forced to flee as drones were spotted searching for and chasing them.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Myanmar (Burma).
Week of 3/2/25: Libya
Libya, a country on the Mediterranean in North Africa, is deeply politically unstable with two rival governments. One is internationally recognized in Tripoli; the other is in the east. Both claim authority to run the country's central bank, a stand-off which could lead to economic collapse.
Only the Lord knows how many Christians are in Libya, but there are a small number of indigenous converts from Islam plus refugees from sub-Saharan Africa, whose goal is to cross the Mediterranean into Europe. Many drown attempting to make the crossing.
Pray for stability for our brothers and sisters in Libya.
Week of 2/23/25: Sudan
Sudan has undergone a severe civil war which began in April 2023 and continues to the present time. In early October 2024, 95 Christians were arrested by the “Sudan Armed Forces” (SAF) in River Nile State in north Sudan. These Christians (25 women, 54 children, and 16 men) were accused of collaborating with the “Rapid Support Forces” (RSF). At the current writing, it is said that the women and children have been released but not the men.
Pray that our brothers and sisters will recover from their ordeal. Pray for the protection of many other Christians displaced by the conflict in Sudan.
Week of 2/16/25: Sri Lanka
Sri Lanka, an island nation at the base of India, is suffering from severe inflation which has improved recently. However, poverty remains widespread.
One-quarter
of households experience food insecurity and consume an inadequate diet. Eight percent of the population are Christian and are among the poorest members of society. In the past 10 years or so they have experienced persecution, even those who are of the traditional well-established Catholic and Orthodox churches.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Sri Lanka.
Week of 2/9/25: Maldives
Pray for the persecuted church in the Maldives, a group of islands in the Indian Ocean and one of the most repressive Muslim-majority countries in the world. Their constitution states that "no law contrary to any tenet of Islam shall be enacted in the Maldives.” Non-Muslim worship is prohibited even by visitors to this island paradise. Their citizens are assumed to be Muslim. There are a few indigenous converts who must remain secret believers or face reprisals from the state and from their families.
Pray for our hidden brothers and sisters in the Maldives, but give praise to God that He knows each one by name!
Week of 2/2/25: Bhutan
The country of Bhutan is a Buddhist-majority South Asian nation in which Christians are not allowed to meet publicly for worship. Churches are not recognized officially by the government, they cannot own property, and evangelism is illegal. They can usually worship in private, however.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Bhutan.
Week of 1/26/25: The Hungry Around the World
It is estimated that over 300 million people around the world are suffering from acute levels of hunger, driven by armed conflict, economic problems, and natural disasters. Many are suffering from enduring food shortages, malnutrition, or stunted growth (children). A majority are Christians, our brothers and sisters in Christ.
Pray for the hungry persecuted church around the world.
Week of 1/19/25: Uzbekistan
Thank God for a rapidly growing church in Uzbekistan and for a recent five-day seminar there for 50 church leaders, strengthening connections, enhancing biblical knowledge, and planning how to respond to the needs of the growing Christian community. Believers face increasing hostility from family members, neighbors, and employers when they begin to follow Christ. Most of the growth in the church is from believers with a Muslim background.
Week of 1/12/25: Afghanistan
As you probably know, Afghanistan under the auspices of the Taliban is under increasing restrictions through its interpretation of Sharia (Islamic) law. Forty percent of children under 5 are so malnourished that their growth is stunted. The scale of the humanitarian disaster taking place under the Taliban is extreme. All women (including Christians) are required to disguise their voices and completely cover their bodies, faces, and hands and are forbidden to go out without a male relative accompanying them. Christian women and girls are particularly vulnerable. All Christians - if it becomes known that they have converted from Islam - will likely be killed for apostasy if their faith is discovered. In addition, they cannot gain employment and must remain in strict hiding.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Afghanistan.
Week of 12/29/24: Bangladesh
Bangladesh is in political turmoil after the Prime Minister fled the country in August. Christians and other religious minorities are facing violence from Islamists, particularly Islamist political parties. They are attempting to use the political vacuum to gain power. Church leaders are seeking assistance from the interim Prime Minister so that the Christians and others will face no deprivation, injustice, or oppression.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Bangladesh and for an end to the unrest.
Week of 12/22/24: Egypt
While generally Christians fare reasonably well in Egypt, some areas experience greater persecution, especially churches in Upper Egypt. In Beni Suef, a church building was destroyed in a massive fire. While the cause continues to be unknown, the building had five floors, offices and a library, and it also housed three schools. No children were injured, but 10 adults were badly burned and hospitalized because of the blaze. Pray for God’s deep care and providence after the loss of so many important facilities. Pray that the church can eventually be rebuilt.
Pray for the persecuted church in Upper Egypt.
Week of 12/15/24: Iraq
There are fewer and fewer Christians in Iraq. They leave because of the instability of the country and the fear of persecution. Before the US-led invasion of Iraq, there were about 1.5 million Christians in Iraq. Sectarian tensions meant that only 700,000 were left by the time the Islamic State seized a third of the country. Christians were among those subjected to violence and most were displaced from their homes. Now it is estimated that only 150,000 to 200,000 are left and this number continues to fall.
Pray for our brothers and sisters in Iraq who have suffered so much.
Week of 12/8/24: Pakistan
Pakistan has extremely harsh “blasphemy laws” which encompass any so-called blasphemy against the Quran or Mohammad or Allah (the Islamic god). The law is very broad and Muslims take advantage of this against Christians. Those accused are often treated violently by mobs, and imprisoned for years, often without trial.
The accusations are usually very flimsy. For example, in two recent cases four people were arrested for destroying pages of the Quran. All four were illiterate and had no idea they had pages of the Quran.
Pray for our imprisoned brothers and sisters in Pakistan.
Week of 11/24/24: Uganda
There are many persecuted Christians (and Muslims) in Uganda, although we are often not aware of it. Here is an example: Juspin, a Muslim woman, just came to Christ after being locked in her home by her husband
for 40 years
. He did not want her to connect with even other Muslim women! She was recently visited by some Christians who shared the Gospel with her,
and she came to Christ!!
While such horrific circumstances abound among Muslims in Uganda, the Gospel is making amazing strides. God is on the move in Uganda! Rejoice over new brothers and sisters in Uganda and elsewhere as God brings in the harvest!
Pray for Christians (and Muslims) who are persecuted in Uganda!
Week of 11/17/24: Democratic Republic of the Congo
In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the northern part (North Kivu) is the worst affected area. At least 84 people were murdered by fighters from Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP) in July and August. At least five more were killed in nearby Itrui province. This violence has been going on for several years. Terrorists also killed at least five others in August and burned down more than 50 houses. The fear is that Islamic violence is spreading to new areas of the country. Pray for the bereaved and that the Lord will restrain this evil.
Week of 11/10/24: Burkina Faso
On August 25, 2024, 26 Christian men were killed during worship in their village church. The Islamists who killed them and claimed responsibility were from a West African terror group affiliated with Al Qaeda. After killing the 26 men, the attackers set fire to houses and stole livestock. The Jihadists now control more than 40% of the nation's territory. Pray for the persecuted church in Burkina Faso, near the border with Mali.
Week of 11/3/24: Mozambique
“Islamic State Mozambique Province” in 2020 abducted and abused Christians, in particular Amina, a 27-year-old woman. By the grace of God, she kept her faith, wasn’t killed as others were, and was released in 2023. Pray for her and others who survived as they continue to heal from their extreme trauma. Since 2017, 6,000 have been killed by the Islamists. Many of those were Christians. Elections occurred last week in this country where the north is experiencing an Islamist insurgency. Pray that people who desire peace will be elected.
Week of 10/27/24: Pakistan
Several issues are critical to the persecuted church in Pakistan.
1) Many young Christian women and girls (as young as 13 or 14) are kidnapped and forced to marry significantly older Muslim men. Once married and often with children it is virtually impossible to get them away from their husbands and divorced. The state usually takes the side of the Muslim men.
2) Normally Christians are illiterate. They are often accused by Muslims of destroying pages from the Quran, which, of course, in most cases they cannot read. They are then arrested, imprisoned and accused of blasphemy. Their punishment is legal under Pakistan Penal Code 295-B. These actions terrify the Christian community because such action is often followed by violence by Muslim extremists. Pray for the Persecuted Church in Pakistan.
Week of 10/20/24: Haiti
Ongoing violence and criminal gangs have taken over most of the capital of Port-au-Prince and the surrounding agricultural areas. 500,000 people have been forced from their homes and in average one person is killed every hour. Furthermore, a missionary couple from the United States, Davy Lloyd and his wife Natalie, were killed in May 2023. Pray for peace and courage to sustain our Christian brothers and sisters in the midst of the violence and killings.
Week of 10/13/24: Laos
Six Christians were arrested and are not yet released in a village in Laos. In June a new village chief was appointed. Previous to June, they were allowed to pray together without harassment. In this primarily Buddhist country, it can be very difficult to pray and worship as Christians. Pray for these six brothers and sisters to be released and that in the future they will be allowed freedom to worship.
Week of 10/6/24: Tunisia
Pray for Christians in Tunisia: Christian converts in Muslim-majority Tunisia face violence from neighbors and family members who reject them and their new faith. Some often keep their faith secret. As they live in danger, pray that God will be present by His Holy Spirit to love, comfort, and protect them.
Week of 9/29/24: Afghanistan
Afghanistan, now under the control of the Taliban, subjected 63 people to public flogging for various crimes in June. Their action underlines Afghanistan's return to hardline Islamist rule since the Taliban returned to power. We do not know how many Christians remain in the country, but if they are discovered they will face death as apostates from Islam. Pray for the Lord to protect and deliver His people from those who plan evil against them.
Week of 9/22/24: Algeria
Algeria is a Muslim-majority country. During a recent election, the incumbent president announced that he would run for a second term. During his presidency, 40 church buildings were closed in Algeria. Pray for the Christians in Algeria to have wisdom as they withstand the closing of their churches and as they find alternative meeting places, usually in small groups in homes.
Week of 9/15/24: Eritrea
Eritrea is a small Communist-dominated country to the north of Ethiopia. Christians are severely persecuted there. Many, especially pastors, are imprisoned. Three pastors have been imprisoned for 20 years (since 2004) without trial. They were abducted from their homes, without charge or trial. They have not been told when or if they will be released. Pray for them and other Christians similarly held. Pray for the persecuted church in Eritrea!
Week of 9/8/24: Nepal
The church in Nepal is undergoing steady growth but is persecuted by the Hindu majority. They encounter restrictions on meeting as Christians and sometimes are brought before the authorities for their faith. They face many unfounded accusations. Four Christians in one province faced trial and were accused of forcing conversions to Christ. They were fined what to them was an exorbitant rate. Pray for them and for Miranda, an Anglican Frontier Missions missionary who serves in Nepal.
Week of 9/1/24: Nigeria
Sporadic killings, persecution, kidnapping and abductions are part of the reality of today's Nigeria. This week we will cover another of the numerous disturbing issues and current happenings, especially in Christian Communities across Nigeria.
This ugly situation and senseless killing began as a movement by Fulani Herdsmen parading their cattle across Southern Nigeria seeking vegetation for their cattle. Little did the Nigerian population know that a greater agenda was for Muslim groups from North Africa to overrun and destroy Christian communities with the pretense of breeding and grazing cattle in various parts of Nigeria, especially in the Northeast, Southeast, and Middle belt regions. Sadly the Fulani-led government under the Buhari administration intentionally empowered them by instituting and passing an “Open Grazing” law that gave these Fulani Herdsmen the impetus to graze at will wherever they found choice vegetation on private properties, farmlands, and family backyard gardens.
Facts established that the Fulani strategy has continued to reveal their intentions to aggressively graze their herds, burn and persecute Christians who get in their way while on this destructive mission with a large number of casualties year after year.
Pray for our Christian brothers and sisters who are simply trying to make a living or who are attempting to feed their families.
Week of 8/25/24: Myanmar (Burma)
Christians in Myanmar, especially in certain tribal areas, are under severe persecution by the Tatmadaw (Myanmar's military). They are regularly hunted down, bombed, and have their homes and churches destroyed. Frequently their pastors are killed. Groups of them flee deep into the jungle to escape torture. In the jungles they often survive by eating leaves, etc. The children suffer inordinately. This has been going on for decades. The Anglican Church has a strong presence there and welcomes short-term missions like SOMA (Sharing of Ministries Abroad). Please pray for our brothers and sisters in Myanmar.
Week of 8/18/24: North Korea
Christians in North Korea are considered to be the most persecuted in the world today.
No display of Christianity is tolerated; all North Koreans are to “worship” their leader, Kim Jong-Un. No gatherings of Christians are allowed under any circumstance and all Koreans are under strict surveillance. No Bibles or Christian books are allowed, although a few Bibles are sometimes smuggled in. If a Christian is caught praying, reading a Bible, or in any way proselytizing, they are either severely punished or imprisoned in harsh labor camps where they are usually worked to death. Please pray for our brothers and sisters in North Korea!
If you wish further information, Mother Valarie suggests
In Order to Live: A North Korean Girl's Journey to Freedom
by Yeonmi Park.
Week of 8/11/24: Nigeria
Christians in Nigeria have been under extreme persecution for a decade now. Although Islamic insurgence and persecution began two decades ago, the North-East, North-West, South-East and the Middle-Belt have suffered unimaginable loss in the hands of these Islamic terrorists.
The peculiarity of these attacks occur in Christian communities where these terrorists intend to take over and expand their area of influence. These Muslim Jihadists, notably called “Boku Haram” (which means “Western education is forbidden”) were reported to have infiltrated into Northern Nigeria from The Niger Republic and the Chad region. They primarily abduct and kill Christian clergy, demand millions of Naira (tens of thousands of dollars) in ransom, kidnap children of Christian faith, burn churches and houses, and decimate villages and communities at will.
In 2014, they kidnapped about 276 teens from a Christian school in Chibok, Borno State in Northern Nigeria; forced them into marriages and also forced them to recant their Christian faith or be beheaded. Over the years, about 100 of these young women have escaped or been rescued from this terrorist group and returned with two or three children born in captivity.
Please cover our precious brothers and sisters with prayer.
Week of 8/4/24: Iran
Pray for Christians in Iran, especially for Christian converts from Islam who are in the notorious Evin Prison in Tehran. Christian converts are often convicted and imprisoned for multiple years for “acting against national security” when all they have done is attend a Christian house church.

Food Giveaway: Prayers for Health and Family
Communications All Saints'
September 16, 2026
Food Giveaway prayer report
We had a good turnout of people on September 12 who came in for prayer. Including a couple of people from All Saints', we totaled 27 overall. Some of the others who came in for prayer were families with four or five people together, including little kids.
We gave out at least five prayer shawls and four Bibles (two Hispanic and two English).
A couple things to note:
Mother Valarie prayed for a woman who wanted prayer for her hurting knee. There was a little bit of a language barrier, but Valarie knew enough Spanish to not only pray for her, but also to understand what she said. The woman went from saying her knee felt good to it felt better to finally excellent, meaning there was no more pain.
Others requested prayers for health and family.
We had a mother and son come in. The son is 24 and was leaving the next week for Army boot camp in North Carolina. They wanted prayers for safety and protection. After he received prayer, the man said he felt better.
A big thanks to Father Patricio for his help in translating for two groups that came in for prayer. It made things so much easier.

Debbie Morrison and Suzy Speare are team members of Kairos #50 scheduled for October 15-18 at the Central Virginia Correctional Unit for Women outside of Richmond.
Kairos is similar to Cursillo or Walk to Emmaus. It includes a three-and-a-half-day weekend program where a trained team of Christians go into the prison to carry God’s message of love and forgiveness to those incarcerated. Would you pray about partnering with us? You can participate in three different ways.
1.     Prayer – Our goal is to have our weekend covered 24/7 in prayer. You can use
this link
to sign up for a 30-minute prayer slot.
2.     Cookies – Each team member is responsible for 27-dozen homemade cookies. Would you bake cookies for us? There are very specific instructions that can be
found here
. Cookies can be brought to the church to the Kairos table in the Atrium or to the Admin Office (weekdays during normal business hours) anytime up until October 13. The final day for delivering cookies is October 13.
3.     Financial Support – Help offset the cost of supplies needed for the weekend. It costs about $150 per prisoner to attend such a weekend. Checks must be made payable to “Kairos of Va” with “CVCU” on the memo line.
Questions? Would you like to learn how you can be a team member for a future Kairos team?  Contact Debbie Morrison at
2157cats@gmail.com
or Suzy Speare at
suzyspeare@aol.com
.

records.body_text:
Communications All Saints'

Why "Formation"?
Communications All Saints'
September 9, 2026
Adults
by Mother Maryanna Stumbaugh
You may have noticed that Adult Education (or Adult Discipleship) is now being referred to as Adult
Formation
.
This may seem innocuous, but it is actually an exciting shift we are making intentionally and in prayerful discernment.
The word “formation” expresses more of a holistic approach, as we seek to be transformed by the power of the Holy Spirit into the image of God. We are called to love the Lord our God not only with our minds but with our whole heart and strength. “Formation” describes this focus — not only intellectual edification, but to include the formation of our beings conforming to Christ.
We intentionally engage this work as one body, one community in Christ. So we invite you to invest in the Adult Formation hour on Sunday mornings from 9:45 a.m. to 10:45 a.m.!

Happy Tuesday, everyone!
I want to share with you the details about the youth watching the Super Bowl this Sunday.
- Students can arrive at the multi purpose room, with food, drinks, and snacks at 6pm.
- Kick-off is scheduled for 6:30.
- We will have several youth leaders present throughout the evening.
- Students will text their parents to come pick them up by 10pm. If a student would like to leave earlier, that's fine. That student will still text a parent to come pick him/her up.
- For students not interested in watching the game, but interested in hanging out and socializing, there will be uno, board games, other card games, table tennis, and fuseball going on. Students can bring a game to play as well.
It will be a fun night with good food, good games, and perhaps a good football game!

Sunday Morning Education Hour- The Holy Spirit: The Lord, the Giver of Life
Guest User
August 10, 2022
We invite you to come explore the Person and work of the Holy Spirit. Each week we will look at a different aspect of the Spirit as He is revealed in both the Old and New Testaments. We will also explore the work of the Spirit in the life of the believer. How does He operate in our life as a community and in our worship? What are spiritual gifts and what place do they have in each believer’s life? These questions and others will be addressed over this 10-week course. Class will meet in the Sanctuary.

Sunday Morning Education Hour- When the Soul Listens: Finding Rest and Direction in Contemplative Prayer
Guest User
August 10, 2022
This book study “provides a solid biblical, theological and historical grounding for one of the most important practices in the Christian life: contemplative prayer.” We will work our way through the text, the practices, and the discussion both as a group and on our own. If this is an area you would like to explore or if you seek to move to a deeper level in this area, plan to join this group. The book,
When the Soul Listens
by Jan Johnson is $14.00 and available the first day the group meets. This group will meet weekly in the Bishop’s Conference Room (on the upper level of the Admin. Wing)

The years are short, but the days are long. All parents need encouragement along the way. Experience Adult Sunday School with
The
Art of Parenting!
This 8-session, video-based study is designed to not only encourage and find new ways to integrate faith into everyday parenting moments, but also to create an environment where moms and dads can shoulder burdens together, celebrate breakthroughs, and relate to one another’s day-to-day parenting journey. Parents of all ages & stages invited!

Tuesday Morning (9:45- 11:30 a.m.)
That You May Believe: A Study of the Gospel of John-
This women’s study will meet at the church on Tuesday mornings for a time of fellowship and study of this beloved gospel. John tells his readers why he wrote his account – that you “may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the son of God,” and “have life in His name.”
No matter where you are in your faith journey, come and let the wonderful truths of this book minister to you. Bring your Bible and a journal or notebook. The group will gather in the Admin. Conference Room at 9:45 for fellowship and start promptly at 10 am

This women’s study will meet at Panera on Thursday Evenings from 7-8:15 for a time of fellowship and study of this beloved gospel. John tells his readers why he wrote his account – that you “may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the son of God,” and “have life in His name.” No matter where you are in your faith journey, come and let the wonderful truths of this book minister to you. WHAT IS FOUNDATIONS FOR MINISTRY
?
An adult Bible study course designed for those willing to make a commitment to daily Bible study.
Intended for those who wish to deepen their understanding of Scripture and our Christian heritage.
It will also equip you to meet the challenges of ministry in the Church and in the world.
Course Format
It is a two-year course of Bible study.  It is divided into two academic years.
Year 1: Old Testament (Beginning September 10, 2023)
Year 2: New Testament (Fall 2024)*
Participants commit to one year of study at a time.
* Participants must complete Year 1 to be eligible to enroll in Year 2.
Weekly Meetings and Small Groups
Each week there will be a short teaching session and small group discussion.
Discussions are based on the weekly homework and include topics such as Bible study skills, personal application, scriptural content, theological concepts, and interpretation of Scripture.
The program requires a commitment to daily study, homework, class attendance, and a willingness to share within a small group.
Foundations groups form a close-knit environment for participants to share what they are learning, and grow in their knowledge of Scripture and their relationship with the Lord and one another.
Beginning on September 10, the class will meet on Sunday evenings from 4-6 p.m. The class will meet at the church from September to June, breaking for 3 weeks at Christmas, 1 week at Easter and 1 week at Memorial Day.
Course Materials
A participant’s workbook ($40/participant/year and only available from All Saints’)
An approved study bible (study notes and tools in these versions are used as part of the study):**
ESV Study Bible
NASB Study Bible
NIV Study Bibles: The NIV Study Bible, 1984 Edition may also be used.
This version is no longer available for sale but may be used if you already own one. Newer versions are not accurate and may not be used for this course.
**Please consult the course leader if you have any questions.
An optional textbook is suggested for each year but not required.
Homework
Homework will take approximately one-half hour per day and is completed ahead of weekly group meetings.
Course Leaders
This class is led by qualified teachers and group leaders. Those teaching have many years of Bible study training and experience. Those leading the small groups are dedicated leaders with both small group and Bible experience.
Attendance
Attending weekly class meetings is an essential part of the class experience. Themes and lessons build on one another from week to week.
Participants must attend at least 80% of the weekly meetings to be eligible for a certificate of completion.
Please contact

or
Jim Morrison
if you have any questions.

Hard Questions about God and Faith: Youth Update (Copy)
Anglican Doma
January 8, 2021
youth
,
education
Hi, Youth Families!
I'm excited to share our plans for Sunday nights as we enter 2021. As we are still right in the middle of the COVID pandemic, it has been a challenging season to plan, prepare, and express ministry in a way that feels normal and worthwhile. There are so many factors to consider and account for in ways that those in ministry haven't had to think about before. The good news is that we are not left to our own, God is with us and he is faithful to help his pastors guide his people.
Beginning Jan. 24 we will dig into a study series titled Can I Ask That? from Fuller Youth Institute. It's part of a program Fuller calls Sticky Faith (a faith in God that lasts). From Fuller Youth Institute: "A recent survey asked leaders of campus-based atheist clubs why they don't believe in God. Their responses were revealing: many had actually been involved in youth ministry during their high school years, and they named the church's failure to engage difficult questions as a key reason they left. Specifically, these young people cited the church's failure to wrestle with issues like the reliability of the biblical text, evolution vs. creation, and the exclusivity of Jesus. These students did not say they left their faith because of the stance their church took on the issues above. They left because the church failed to address them at all. When tough questions were addressed, the answers were found to be vague and superficial."
We are not looking to be vague or superficial here at All Saints' Youth. We want to engage issues and topics that you are struggling with, knowing that in that struggle and tension God is with us the whole time and will increase and strengthen our faith. It doesn't mean that we will solve every problem we encounter or have all of the answers to every question raised. It does mean that we will be challenged, pushed, and forced to live with the tension of saying 'I don't know'. But we know that it is better to say 'I don't know' instead of avoiding tough questions and issues. We know that the Holy Spirit will guide us and give us God's peace in spite of what we may think or feel. I'm excited to start this journey with you and I look forward to where God takes us as we push ourselves to go deeper with him!
Stay tuned for an email from me early next week with info for purchasing the book and Sunday night meeting details!
Thanks so much!
Jedd+

Please come twice a month on Tuesday evenings, beginning September 22, by Zoom (and on occasion at Panera for a parents night out!!) from 7-8 p.m. for discussion of a beloved bestseller,
Liturgy of the Ordinary: Sacred Practices of Everyday Life
by Tish Harrison Warren. In the overlooked moments and routines of our day, we can become aware of God's presence in surprising ways. How do we embrace the sacred in the ordinary and the ordinary in the sacred? Framed around one ordinary day, this book explores daily life through the lens of liturgy, small practices, and habits that form us. Each chapter looks at something―making the bed, brushing her teeth, losing her keys―that the author does every day. Drawing from the diversity of her life as a campus minister, Anglican priest, friend, wife, and mother, Tish Harrison Warren opens up a practical theology of the everyday. Each activity is related to a spiritual practice as well as an aspect of our Sunday worship. Come and discover the holiness of your every day.

Anglican Doma
August 25, 2020
youth
(Below is the email Jedd+ sent to youth and parents about a new Bible study starting via Zoom on Thursday, Aug 19. If you miss a week, no worries! Jedd+ will send out the link for each recorded Zoom session to the email list each week. Sign up
here
.)
Parents and Youth,
I am so excited to announce the study I will be starting with our Thursday night Bible study via Zoom.
I have been reviewing a new opportunity to study the Bible together. It is called the Bible Project. You can view an intro
video
here.
The
website
provides more details, as well. The general idea is that this is a graduate-level Bible class online. These classes are designed to equip learners with study tools that foster deep engagement with the biblical story. I have no doubt that our mature middle school and high school students will be able to engage and follow along with the videos and discussions. Together we will learn how to study the Bible as we learn more about the Bible.
With that in mind, we'll start with the course "
Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
" and will work through that over the next few months. We all know Bible stories but do you know the story of the Bible?
We'll do the introduction this Thursday, Aug 20. Encourage your students to participate. Although the course does build on itself, it is okay to pop in and out as schedules allow.
To help with consistency, I have a few recommendations.
1) I will record each Thursday night Zoom session with video and discussion. I will send out the link to that Zoom after each session, so your teens can watch it at their leisure.
2) Consider creating a free account at the
Bible Project website
for your teen(s) to review the materials and access additional resources. Each teen can certainly have their own account with parental permission.
3) Parents, if you have any time, I encourage you to follow along on your independent study to engage in conversations with your teens.
There is no expectation of homework or coming in prepared. Just show up.
Questions?
Let me know!
Jedd+

records.body_text:
Anglican Doma

Wednesday Evening - Embrace the Journey
Anglican Doma
August 21, 2020
Adults
CLASS IS FULL - Registration is closed
We will be doing an introductory session on Wednesday, September 16 at 7 p.m. for those who would like to explore this topic or ask questions before starting the full course.
Covid19 has turned our world upside down; we now talk of our “new normal.” There has been a lot of reports on the number of deaths as a result of this pandemic.  As much as most of us would rather not think about it, aging and dying are not only normal but universal. Not only will all of us die one day, but many of us will care for parents, family, and friends going through the aging and dying process. All Saints’ will be offering a course this fall on aging and dying.
Embrace the Journey is an 8-week adult education series designed to help you and your church understand and apply God’s Word to end of life issues.  Topics include the biblical view of life, preparing for the golden years, advance directives and advanced care plans, health care, hastening death, funeral plans and the role of the church in suffering and grief. Other sections can be added as needed. Each week’s session has a short video followed by group discussion. Registration is required; please register using the button below, so we can send you class information and have a Participant Guide ready for you. Each Participant Guide is $20 and includes the Finishing Life: Preparing for the End of Life booklet and full scripts from the video teaching. Couples can purchase an extra copy of Finishing Life for $5 each. This course will meet via Zoom on Wednesday evenings from 7-9 p.m. beginning September 23. If you have further questions please call or email Desiree Barker at the church office 703-670-0093 or at
dbarker@allsaintswoodbridge.org

records.author: Anglican Doma
records.body_text:
Anglican Doma
October 22, 2020
Common Recovery
Anglican Doma
October 22, 2020
At
Common Recovery
our goal is to
shower Prince William County with a message of hope; cultivating a community of recovery through recovery services, spiritual growth and peer housing. Evangelizing the working poor and raising up effective leaders from the least, the last and the lost.
This  program is known for its message of recovery for those who are hopelessly struggling with alcohol/drug addiction and have found no other way out.
It is our desire to reach out to those who are still suffering and lost.
We are here to pass on what was freely given to us —
“a message of hope.”
We were once on a path of destruction ourselves – addicted to alcohol and drugs. Alone in that dark pit of misery; we were desperate for change; but not able to stop! Our hearts cry was that God would stop the madness! That He would deliver us from that lifestyle that only promised death.
As recovered addicts ourselves, we understand & can help. It’s about staying clean & sober but that’s not all there’s more– it’s about getting our lives back as well!
Download a brochure here.

records.author: Anglican Doma
records.body_text:
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
StreetLight Community Outreach Ministries
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
After handing one woman a check for her overdue rent, she broke down in tears of relief. Between sobs, she told us for months she had been overcome with anxiety about where her children would sleep if they were evicted from their apartment. She had worked as a maid for a family that was forced to lay her off during the pandemic, which left her with no income and ineligible for unemployment. Sadly, her story is not uncommon. The National Low Income Housing Coalition recently announced 30-40 million Americans would face eviction by the end of the year - a direct result of the economic slowdown and massive job losses caused by the coronavirus outbreak .

records.author: Anglican Doma
heading_structure: h1: Missionary Support: Global Mobilization Ministries (the Rev. Canon Dr. Alison Barfoot)
records.body_text:
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
Missionary Support: Global Mobilization Ministries (the Rev. Canon Dr. Alison Barfoot)
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
The Rev. Canon Alison L. Barfoot serves as the Assistant for International Relations to the Archbishop of Uganda. This ministry represents the cutting edge of mission strategy in the church today, for Uganda is not only a mission field—it is also an incredibly ripe mission force with which we can partner to fulfill the Great Commission (Matt. 28:16-20). The focus of Alison’s work is to mobilize Ugandans to bless the nations.
Visit the Global Mobilization Ministry
website
.

records.body_text:

Anglican Fund for Relief and Development (ARDF)
Anglican Doma
October 19, 2020
Inspired by God’s radical grace, the Anglican Relief and Development Fund exists to empower Anglicans in the developing world to show the love of Christ to those in need in their own communities: Clean water for the thirsty, jobs for the poor, education for children, food for the hungry, and hope for those without hope.

LENT 2024: TRUE FASTING
from ACNA’s Matthew 25 Initiative
At the Matthew 25 Initiative, our desire is to see the unseen and the marginalized treasured.
And this Lenten season, we will be telling the stories of the least of these through 40 days of Anglican-informed, inspiring, beautiful, and theologically robust engagement pieces — in the vein of the church's traditional disciplines of Lent:  prayer, fasting, and almsgiving.
For our third year of Lent, we once again invite you to join us on a journey of normalizing Anglican justice and mercy by thoughtfully engaging in this historic Christian season of prayer, fasting, and almsgiving – this time, through the lens of Isaiah 58:6-12.
Check it out
here
.  It is a free devotional you can sign up to have delivered directly to your email each day.

Guest User
